title: Multi-method simulation modelling of circular manufacturing systems for enhanced decision-making
author: Roci, Salehi, et al.

steps.title: Select simulation platform
steps.instruction: Use a Java‑based simulation development platform that supports agent‑based (AB), discrete‑event (DE) and system‑dynamics (SD) modelling; the authors used AnyLogic.

steps.title: Define stakeholder agents and behaviours
steps.instruction: Create the set of CMS stakeholder‑agents (Manufacturer, ServiceProvider, Customer, Recycler) and assign a modelling construct to each: DE process flowcharts for Manufacturer, ServiceProvider and Recycler; AB statecharts for Customer (and Technician) where event‑ and time‑ordering is critical; SD stock‑and‑flow diagrams inside the Customer agent to capture continuous revenue and GHG flows.

steps.title: Specify service subscription options
steps.instruction: Model the white‑goods‑as‑a‑service offering by defining three subscription packages – Gold, Silver and Bronze – each with distinct service level, washing‑machine type and subscription flexibility attributes.

steps.title: Define relationships among agents
steps.instruction: Establish unidirectional or bidirectional connections between stakeholder‑agents to represent physical (products), information (order requests) and financial (revenue, cost) flows; implement these connections as agent interfaces consisting of attributes, methods, ports or messages.

steps.title: Set up GIS simulation environment
steps.instruction: Place all stakeholder‑agents on a Geographic Information System (GIS) map according to their real‑world locations so that distances can be retrieved for transport‑cost and greenhouse‑gas‑emission calculations.

steps.title: Create agent populations
steps.instruction: In AnyLogic, create three agent categories: stakeholder‑agents and product‑agents as populations, and order‑agents as agent types only. Populate stakeholder‑agents with a given number of agents (exact count defined by the case study). Initialise the product‑agent population as empty; it will be filled dynamically by the Manufacturer agent at runtime. Define order‑agent types (ProductRequest, ServiceRequest, TreatmentRequest) to be instantiated dynamically when a stakeholder‑agent places an order.

steps.title: Model product journey
steps.instruction: Represent each washing machine as an individual product‑agent that remains in continuous communication with the stakeholder‑agents throughout its multiple lifecycles (manufacture, deployment, maintenance, refurbishment, end‑of‑life).

steps.title: Define performance measurement variables
steps.instruction: Specify the set of variables to collect statistics at both agent and system levels, covering economic metrics (lifecycle costs, revenues, profits), environmental metrics (lifecycle impact, GHG emissions) and technical metrics (quality, quantity and timing of product return).

steps.title: Verify and validate the model
steps.instruction: Perform verification and validation using animation, comparison with analytical models, degenerate and extreme‑condition tests, and face validity; embed animations in AnyLogic to check logic; collaborate with the white‑goods manufacturer and service providers to review results.
